subject: Urban Planning
title: Circular Cities: Waste as Resource
description: A 60-second lesson on Circular Cities: Waste as Resource.

hook.text: Amsterdam aims to be fully circular by 2050 — a city where nothing is wasted and every output becomes an input.

buildup.text: In a circular city, construction debris becomes building material. Sewage becomes fertilizer. Heat from data centers warms homes.

discovery.text: Amsterdam's circular strategy maps every material flow in the city — tracking where resources enter and where waste exits.

twist.text: A circular economy requires redesigning supply chains. Companies must take back products at end of life. Few are willing.

climax.text: If every city adopted circular principles, global resource consumption would drop 28%. The model exists. The will doesn't yet.

punchline.text: No waste. Everything reused. One city is trying. The rest are watching.

quiz.question: What is Amsterdam's circular city goal?
options: To become fully circular by 2050, eliminating all waste through reuse
To power the entire city with circular wind turbines by 2040
To replace all roads with circular pedestrian paths by 2035
